10.1002_smll.202509324: The electrochemical carbon monoxide reduction reaction (CORR) represents a promising approach for the conversion of CO into acetate. However, the efficiency and selectivity of CO‐to‐acetate conversion are hindered by the competing formation of other products. Here, a Cu‐MFU‐4l‐F catalyst is reported that preserves mixed‐valence Cu species through the introduction of halogens and a precise Cu─N 3 coordination structure, facilitating efficient CORR with a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 73.2% for acetate in a flow cell. Furthermore, the selectivity for acetate remained stable over 140 h in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer. The X‐ray absorption spectroscopy reveals that the coordination environment around Cu is retained during the catalysis. In situ ATR‐FTIRS indicates that the introduction of fluorine enhanced surface * CO adsorption and key intermediate * OCCOH formation, facilitates asymmetric C─C coupling, and improves the selectivity for acetate.
10.1016_j.desal.2026.120556: Cooling is as critical as heating in membrane distillation (MD) systems, yet it has received far less attention. The inherent cooling provided by incoming feedwater, termed “replenishment cooling”, becomes increasingly limited at higher recoveries as less fresh feedwater enters the system. Although replenishment cooling has been implemented at pilot scale, few studies have quantified the cooling potential of replenishment cooling or its ability to address the cooling deficit of heat-pump MD systems. In this study, we evaluate replenishment cooling alone and replenishment and heat-pump cooling. Results show that replenishment cooling alone is effective up to water recoveries of 40–60%, depending on feedwater temperature, but becomes insufficient beyond this range. On the other hand, combined replenishment and heat-pump cooling maintains effective cooling across the full recovery range and enables treatment of feedwaters from seawater to high-salinity produced water, achieving concentrations pertinent to minimum liquid discharge (MLD) and zero liquid discharge (ZLD). We also identify a positive feedback loop between two cooling approaches: the heat pump lowers the temperature on the condensation side, increasing the rate of water production, which in turn raises the flow of cool incoming feedwater, further improving cooling. This synergy allows the combined system to achieve the highest water production rates across all operating conditions, without the need for additional cooling equipment, making it a practical strategy for high-recovery MD operation.
10.1016_j.jsamd.2026.101186: Biodegradable synthetic polymer, poly(vinyl alcohol), PVA and polysaccharide-based blend electrolytes offer high ionic conductivity, good mechanical strength, better electrode-electrolyte contact and wide electrochemical stability window (ESW). In this research, plasticized polymer-biopolymer blend electrolyte (PBBE) membranes based on [PVA-sodium alginate (NaAlg)-zinc triflate] and ionic liquid (IL), [EMIM][TFSI] have been prepared using the solution casting method. The formulated samples were characterized using XRD, FESEM, Infrared (IR) spectroscopy, impedance spectroscopy (EIS), transference number (TN) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) measurements. XRD and FESEM results demonstrate that the loading of ionic liquid significantly modifies the crystalline phase and surface morphology of the prepared samples. IR results confirm the interactions between EMIM + /Zn 2+ ions with OH/COO - functional groups of PVA-NaAlg blend. The PBBE membrane loaded with 60 wt.% IL (i.e. PSZnIL#60) has the maximum ionic conductivity of 5.2 × 10 -3 S cm -1 , with TN of 0.99. Loading IL improves the ESW of PBPE membranes significantly. The temperature-dependent ionic conductivity analysis followed Arrhenius-type behavior for all PBBE membranes. A Zn-ion hybrid capacitor (ZIHC) based on PSZnIL#60 delivered a specific capacitance of 306.66-50.70 F g -1 , energy density of 161.96–14.20 Wh kg -1 , and power density of 195–3408 W k g -1 across current densities of 0.1–2.4 A g -1 . The stability test conducted at a current density of 1.2 A g -1 revealed that the device achieved a high coulombic efficiency of 98% and maintained 87% of its initial capacity after 5000 charge–discharge cycles, highlighting its strong potential for energy storage applications. • IR results reveal the interactions of EMIM + /Zn 2+ with OH/COO - of PVA-NaAlg blend • IL acts as a plasticizer, weakening the Zn 2+ –alginate bonds as evidenced by XRD & FESEM • IL loading improves the ESW and PSZnIL#60 membrane has the σ dc = 5.2 × 10 -3 S cm -1 • The ZIHC device exhibits C s = 306.66 F g -1 , E d = 161.96 Wh kg -1 with P d = 195 W kg -1 • ZIHC retained 87% capacity with 98% Coulombic efficiency after 5000 cycles of charge-discharge
10.1021_acsenergylett.6c02308: Existing alloy anodes suffer from high redox potentials and sluggish Li atomic kinetics, limiting the energy density and rate capability of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Herein, we report a well-designed Li3Ga2 alloy anode that simultaneously delivers an ultralow Li deposition potential (0.007 V vs. Li+/Li) and fast Li atomic diffusion kinetics (2.0 × 10–8 cm2 s–1). The high Li atomic diffusivity primarily originates from moderate Li/Ga antisite mixing, stabilizing the anode-solid electrolyte interface and enabling a high critical current density of 24 mA cm–2 in ASSLBs. Coupled with a LiCoO2 cathode, the ASSLB delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 96.5% and an ultralong cycle life of 2000 cycles at room temperature, with a high output voltage of 3.84 V, outperforming state-of-the-art alloy-based counterparts. A practical all-solid-state pouch cell employing the LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode also delivers outstanding cycling stability. This work redefines alloy anode design principles through synergistic optimization of Li deposition potential and Li atomic diffusivity.
